consensus_findings.description: Critical: Expired-lease takeover is conditioned on the absence of contradictory live-process evidence, but the plan never defines what process identity is recorded, where that record lives, how PID reuse or host identity is handled, or how the takeover checker distinguishes a live old writer from stale process metadata. The registry schema has no process token, and the only related statement says the controller persists unspecified non-authoritative process context. Implementers must therefore either fail every expired takeover as indeterminate or silently omit the zombie check that the fencing model relies on.

Critical: The spec requires a changed head SHA to invalidate an operator delivery-stage disposition, but the durable operatorOverride contract stores only actor, selected_stage, reason, and recorded_at. It does not bind the override to the base/head SHAs or a classification digest. After an ambiguous PR is overridden as proposal, new code can be pushed while the persisted override still selects planning-only validation and preserve-active-change cleanup, and the executor has no durable value against which to detect staleness.

Critical: lease release-owner clears every exact-owner lease without the quarantine rule applied to release-session or unsafe per-entry release. A recovery operator can therefore clear a live or crashed owner's bulk leases while preserved dirty/non-durable worktrees remain recovery_required=false, making them ordinary-acquire eligible and reopening both concurrent-writer and silent-dirty-state adoption risks.

Nit: Package worktrees are required to be disposed after integration only when remotely durable, but the plan never states which remote ref proves durability for a child branch or when the parent feature branch must be pushed relative to child disposal. Existing package branches are local integration children and are not necessarily pushed under their own names, so checking each entry's branch would quarantine successful packages even when their commits are reachable from the pushed parent feature branch.

Nit: Holding the registry lock across Git removal and registry deletion prevents concurrent acquisition but does not make the two side effects atomic. A crash after git worktree remove succeeds and before the registry entry is deleted leaves a live leased orphan entry; the contract defines idempotency only when both the entry and checkout are absent and does not specify owner-fenced reconciliation for this one-sided state.

Nit: recovery adopt says it atomically acquires a manual lease but does not define the resulting session_id, phase, TTL/timestamps, recovery reason clearing, exit codes, or JSON output, even though every one of those fields is mandatory or operationally relevant in schema v2. The safety-critical adoption path is therefore less specified than ordinary acquire.

The revised plan correctly separates retention, activity, and recovery quarantine, and it carries one acquisition-specific lease id through mutation boundaries so same-owner resumes cannot revive an expired writer.

The delivery classifier fails closed on incomplete primary evidence and conflicting markers, while author-vendor claims remain unverified routing evidence rather than authentication; these are sound safety boundaries.
